I think there is an issue in a loop-carried tensor bufferization; it's doing extra allocations that can be avoided. 

The following dispatch hits assertion of `Assertion memref::CastOp::areCastCompatible(buffer.getType(), type) && "scf.while op bufferization: cast incompatible"' failed.` with `tools/iree-opt --split-input-file --pass-pipeline='hal.executable(hal.executable.variant(iree-codegen-linalg-to-spirv-pipeline))'`:

```mlir
hal.executable private @forward_dispatch_14 {
  hal.executable.variant public @vulkan_spirv_fb, target = <"vulkan", "vulkan-spirv-fb", {spv.target_env = #spv.target_env<#spv.vce<v1.3, [Shader, GroupNonUniform, GroupNonUniformVote, GroupNonUniformArithmetic, GroupNonUniformBallot, GroupNonUniformShuffle, GroupNonUniformShuffleRelative], [SPV_KHR_storage_buffer_storage_class]>, SwiftShader:CPU, #spv.resource_limits<max_compute_workgroup_size = [128, 128, 64], subgroup_size = 4, cooperative_matrix_properties_nv = []>>}> {
    hal.executable.export public @forward_dispatch_14 ordinal(0) layout(#hal.executable.layout<push_constants = 0, sets = [#hal.descriptor_set.layout<0, bindings = [#hal.descriptor_set.binding<0, storage_buffer>, #hal.descriptor_set.binding<1, storage_buffer>, #hal.descriptor_set.binding<2, storage_buffer>]>]>)
    builtin.module {
      func.func @forward_dispatch_14() {
        %c36864 = arith.constant 36864 : index
        %c234512576 = arith.constant 234512576 : index
        %c4352 = arith.constant 4352 : index
        %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
        %cst = arith.constant 0.000000e+00 : f32
        %0 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(0) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c0) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:1x9216xf32>
        %1 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(1) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c4352) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:9216x4096xf32>
        %2 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(1) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c234512576) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:1x4096xf32>
        %3 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(2) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c36864) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<writeonly:1x4096xf32>
        %4 = flow.dispatch.tensor.load %0, offsets = [0, 0], sizes = [1, 9216], strides = [1, 1] : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:1x9216xf32> -> tensor<1x9216xf32>
        %5 = flow.dispatch.tensor.load %1, offsets = [0, 0], sizes = [9216, 4096], strides = [1, 1] : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:9216x4096xf32> -> tensor<9216x4096xf32>
        %6 = flow.dispatch.tensor.load %2, offsets = [0, 0], sizes = [1, 4096], strides = [1, 1] : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:1x4096xf32> -> tensor<1x4096xf32>
        %7 = linalg.init_tensor [1, 4096] : tensor<1x4096xf32>
        %8 = linalg.matmul ins(%4, %5 : tensor<1x9216xf32>, tensor<9216x4096xf32>) outs(%6 : tensor<1x4096xf32>) -> tensor<1x4096xf32>
        %9 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0, d1)>, affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0, d1)>], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel"]} ins(%8 : tensor<1x4096xf32>) outs(%7 : tensor<1x4096xf32>) {
        ^bb0(%arg0: f32, %arg1: f32):
          %10 = arith.cmpf ugt, %arg0, %cst : f32
          %11 = arith.select %10, %arg0, %cst : f32
          linalg.yield %11 : f32
        } -> tensor<1x4096xf32>
        flow.dispatch.tensor.store %9, %3, offsets = [0, 0], sizes = [1, 4096], strides = [1, 1] : tensor<1x4096xf32> -> !flow.dispatch.tensor<writeonly:1x4096xf32>
        return
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The above input won't hit assertion with `tools/iree-opt --iree-codegen-iree-comprehensive-bufferize` (given that we use different allocation functions as the default in the pass), but it triggers extra allocations for `%8`, given that `%8` is bound to `%arg2` in the loop which yields:

https://gist.githubusercontent.com/antiagainst/60168124bf3a0354a85e216c44aed65b/raw/0f107f3ed2f2efd9edece7553eb474a05abff09a/bufferization-alloc.mlir


(The cancelling `memref.cast` pair would hit assert if we are using a different address space, which is the case for GPU.) 

I think `%9` can be assigned to the buffer for `%3`, so write to `%arg2` can use `%3`'s buffer, while reading of `%arg2` can use `%2'` buffer. Not sure how we can achieve this in the current bufferization patterns though.

@matthias-springer @MaheshRavishankar any thoughts?

I think the issue might be somewhere else.

The input IR is doing this 
```
        %6 = flow.dispatch.tensor.load %2, offsets = [0, 0], sizes = [1, 4096], strides = [1, 1] : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:1x4096xf32> -> tensor<1x4096xf32>
        %8 = linalg.matmul ins(%4, %5 : tensor<1x9216xf32>, tensor<9216x4096xf32>) outs(%6 : tensor<1x4096xf32>) -> tensor<1x4096xf32>
```

where `%6` is a `readonly`. That shouldnt be happening. Do you have the IR just before/after dispatch region formation. THe `outs` of this operation needs to be fused into the dispatch.

> where %6 is a readonly. That shouldnt be happening. 

For tensors the `outs` parameters in linalg ops are just for initial values so it should be fine? (I might not catch up on all the details about read/write and how we link buffers together at the flow levels though..)

> Do you have the IR just before/after dispatch region formation.

Here is the input before the dispatch region formation:
https://gist.githubusercontent.com/antiagainst/60168124bf3a0354a85e216c44aed65b/raw/6859fa83cbf7044838bbfc4b02100c999c5c17ae/dispatch-region.mlir

> THe outs of this operation needs to be fused into the dispatch.

`%6` is a large constant tensor so maybe that's why it's not fused into the dispatch. 


I feel one way to fix this is to shift the initial value `%6` on `linalg.matmul` to the fused `linalg.generic` and do the addition first in the `linalg.generic`.

We can split the issue into two.
1) The way the IR is should be handled by the bufferization without crashes.
2) Feeding a constant into the `outs` of a matmul is bad form. The input is basically doing a bias-add by broadcasting the bias into the `outs` and using this. Fixing that would get around (1).

```
I feel one way to fix this is to shift the initial value %6 on linalg.matmul to the fused linalg.generic and do the addition first in the linalg.generic.
```

Thats a very specific clean up. You need to check that the `linalg.generic` is just an add to get around this. But we've seen this enough times that it might be worth just biting the bullet on this. So as one of the very first "input clean up passes" in Flow, convert `outs` that are not `linalg.fill` to op + `linalg.generic` which does the add. The elementwise fusion should handle things automatically.

issue.body:
### What happened?

Lowering to vulkan with M1 triple or when no target triples are specified(work for ampere triples), seems to be breaking due to some memref cast issues. When lowering on alexnet and Bert.

### Steps to reproduce your issue

## Alexnet

**Command:**
```bash
wget https://storage.googleapis.com/iree-shared-files/nod-perf/stanley/vulkan_repro/alexnet_torch_linalg.mlir

iree-compile --iree-input-type=none --iree-vm-bytecode-module-output-format=flatbuffer-binary --iree-hal-target-backends=vulkan --iree-mlir-to-vm-bytecode-module --iree-llvm-embedded-linker-path=iree-lld --mlir-print-debuginfo --mlir-print-op-on-diagnostic=false --iree-llvm-target-cpu-features=host alexnet_torch_linalg.mlir -o /tmp/alexnet_vulkan.vmfb
```

**Expected output:**
```bash
/tmp/alexnet_torch_linalg.mlir
:174:11: error: 'memref.cast' op operand type 'memref<1x2048xf32, affine_map<(d0, d1)[s0, s1, s2] -> (d0 * s1 + s0 + d1 * s2)>>' and result type 'memref<1x2048xf32, 6>' are cast incompatible
    %69 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [#map6, #map4], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel"]} ins(%68 : tensor<1x4096xf32>) outs(%64 : tensor<1x4096xf32>) {
          ^
/tmp/alexnet_torch_linalg.mlir
:9:3: note: called from
  func.func @forward(%arg0: tensor<1x3x224x224xf32>) -> tensor<1x1000xf32> {
  ^
/tmp/alexnet_torch_linalg.mlir
:174:11: error: failed to run translation of source executable to target executable for backend #hal.executable.target<"vulkan", "vulkan-spirv-fb", {spv.target_env = #spv.target_env<#spv.vce<v1.3, [Shader, GroupNonUniform, GroupNonUniformVote, GroupNonUniformArithmetic, GroupNonUniformBallot, GroupNonUniformShuffle, GroupNonUniformShuffleRelative], [SPV_KHR_storage_buffer_storage_class]>, SwiftShader:CPU, #spv.resource_limits<max_compute_workgroup_size = [128, 128, 64], subgroup_size = 4, cooperative_matrix_properties_nv = []>>}>
    %69 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [#map6, #map4], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel"]} ins(%68 : tensor<1x4096xf32>) outs(%64 : tensor<1x4096xf32>) {
```

## BERT

**Command:**
```bash
wget https://storage.googleapis.com/iree-shared-files/nod-perf/stanley/vulkan_repro/bert_torch_linalg.mlir

iree-compile --iree-input-type=none --iree-vm-bytecode-module-output-format=flatbuffer-binary --iree-hal-target-backends=vulkan --iree-mlir-to-vm-bytecode-module --iree-llvm-embedded-linker-path=iree-lld --mlir-print-debuginfo --mlir-print-op-on-diagnostic=false --iree-llvm-target-cpu-features=host bert_torch_linalg.mlir -o /tmp/bert_torch_vulkan.vmfb
```

**Expected output:**
```bash
/tmp/bert_torch_linalg.mlir:3475:12: error: 'memref.cast' op operand type 'memref<1x256xf32, affine_map<(d0, d1)[s0, s1, s2] -> (d0 * s1 + s0 + d1 * s2)>>' and result type 'memref<1x256xf32, 6>' are cast incompatible
    %874 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [#map1, #map2], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel"]} ins(%873 : tensor<1x768xf32>) outs(%869 : tensor<1x768xf32>) {
           ^
/tmp/bert_torch_linalg.mlir:23:3: note: called from
  func.func @forward(%arg0: tensor<1x128xi64>) -> tensor<1x2xf32> {
  ^
/tmp/bert_torch_linalg.mlir3475:12: error: failed to run translation of source executable to target executable for backend #hal.executable.target<"vulkan", "vulkan-spirv-fb", {spv.target_env = #spv.target_env<#spv.vce<v1.3, [Shader, GroupNonUniform, GroupNonUniformVote, GroupNonUniformArithmetic, GroupNonUniformBallot, GroupNonUniformShuffle, GroupNonUniformShuffleRelative], [SPV_KHR_storage_buffer_storage_class]>, SwiftShader:CPU, #spv.resource_limits<max_compute_workgroup_size = [128, 128, 64], subgroup_size = 4, cooperative_matrix_properties_nv = []>>}>
    %874 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [#map1, #map2], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel"]} ins(%873 : tensor<1x768xf32>) outs(%869 : tensor<1x768xf32>) {
```

    %4 = flow.dispatch.tensor.load %0, offsets = [0, 0], sizes = [1, 9216], strides = [1, 1] : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:1x9216xf32> -> tensor<1x9216xf32>

The above input won't hit assertion with `tools/iree-opt --iree-codegen-iree-comprehensive-bufferize` (given that we use different allocation functions as the default in the pass), but it triggers extra allocations for `%8`, given that `%8` is bound to `%arg2` in the loop which yields:

https://gist.githubusercontent.com/antiagainst/60168124bf3a0354a85e216c44aed65b/raw/0f107f3ed2f2efd9edece7553eb474a05abff09a/bufferization-alloc.mlir


(The cancelling `memref.cast` pair would hit assert if we are using a different address space, which is the case for GPU.) 

I think `%9` can be assigned to the buffer for `%3`, so write to `%arg2` can use `%3`'s buffer, while reading of `%arg2` can use `%2'` buffer. Not sure how we can achieve this in the current bufferization patterns though.

@matthias-springer @MaheshRavishankar any thoughts?

I think the issue might be somewhere else.

The input IR is doing this 
```
        %6 = flow.dispatch.tensor.load %2, offsets = [0, 0], sizes = [1, 4096], strides = [1, 1] : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:1x4096xf32> -> tensor<1x4096xf32>
        %8 = linalg.matmul ins(%4, %5 : tensor<1x9216xf32>, tensor<9216x4096xf32>) outs(%6 : tensor<1x4096xf32>) -> tensor<1x4096xf32>
```

where `%6` is a `readonly`. That shouldnt be happening. Do you have the IR just before/after dispatch region formation. THe `outs` of this operation needs to be fused into the dispatch.

> where %6 is a readonly. That shouldnt be happening. 

For tensors the `outs` parameters in linalg ops are just for initial values so it should be fine? (I might not catch up on all the details about read/write and how we link buffers together at the flow levels though..)

> Do you have the IR just before/after dispatch region formation.

Here is the input before the dispatch region formation:
https://gist.githubusercontent.com/antiagainst/60168124bf3a0354a85e216c44aed65b/raw/6859fa83cbf7044838bbfc4b02100c999c5c17ae/dispatch-region.mlir

> THe outs of this operation needs to be fused into the dispatch.

`%6` is a large constant tensor so maybe that's why it's not fused into the dispatch. 


I feel one way to fix this is to shift the initial value `%6` on `linalg.matmul` to the fused `linalg.generic` and do the addition first in the `linalg.generic`.

We can split the issue into two.
1) The way the IR is should be handled by the bufferization without crashes.
2) Feeding a constant into the `outs` of a matmul is bad form. The input is basically doing a bias-add by broadcasting the bias into the `outs` and using this. Fixing that would get around (1).

```
I feel one way to fix this is to shift the initial value %6 on linalg.matmul to the fused linalg.generic and do the addition first in the linalg.generic.
```

Thats a very specific clean up. You need to check that the `linalg.generic` is just an add to get around this. But we've seen this enough times that it might be worth just biting the bullet on this. So as one of the very first "input clean up passes" in Flow, convert `outs` that are not `linalg.fill` to op + `linalg.generic` which does the add. The elementwise fusion should handle things automatically.
